name: Engalm
kurzbeschreibung: The Engalm in the Großer Ahornboden: Tyrol's oldest alpine village with over 1,000 years of dairy farming tradition, a show dairy, and 2,200 centuries-old sycamore maples.
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Ende Oktober täglich 08:30–18:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional Almdorf Eng (often simply referred to as Engalm) sits at 1,250 metres above sea level in the idyllic valley head of the Rißtal in the heart of the Naturpark Karwendel. Administratively belonging to the Tyrolean municipality of Vomp, this ensemble forms the oldest documented alpine village in Tyrol, boasting more than a millennium of uninterrupted alpine pastoral tradition. Nestled within the natural monument Großer Ahornboden, where more than 2,200 gnarled sycamore maple trees up to 600 years old take root beneath the sheer limestone faces of the Karwendel-Nordkette, the Eng ranks among the most breathtaking natural and cultural landscapes in the entire Alps.

History & Cheese Tradition

Already in the early Middle Ages, farming families from the Inntal valley used this fertile pasture at the foot of the Spritzkarspitze; the Eng was first recorded in official documents in 1523 as a communal pasture. To this day, the pasture is managed by the local farming cooperative Agrargemeinschaft Eng. The heritage-protected village comprises around 30 historical wooden log cabins, barns, a chapel, and a traditional alpine inn. During the alpine summer from June to September, around 500 dairy cows graze here. Fresh hay milk is processed on-site in copper vats following time-honoured recipes at the glazed Schaukäserei Eng. The award-winning Enger Bergkäse has garnered multiple gold medals at international cheese olympiads. Because the Rißtal is encircled by sheer rock ranges, the valley forms a geographical curiosity: by car, the Eng can only be accessed via German territory (Bavaria via Lenggries or Wallgau).

Visit & Getting There

The alpine village, the farm shop, and the show dairy are open daily from mid-May to late October (All Saints' Day) from 08:30 to 18:00. Admission to the entire alpine village, the show dairy, and the alpine museum is free of charge. A moderate toll is charged for the 14-kilometre scenic road Hinterriß–Eng (approx. €7.00 per car, €5.00 for motorcycles, free for bicycles). Getting there by car: from Munich/Bad Tölz via Lenggries, Sylvensteinspeicher, and Vorderriß to Hinterriß; from Tyrol via Achenpass or via Seefeld/Mittenwald to Vorderriß. The large car park P10 is situated at the valley head. By public transport: from Munich on the Bayerische Regiobahn (BRB) to Lenggries station, from where the RVO-Bergsteigerbus Linie 9569 runs directly to the Eng several times a day during the summer months.

Tips

From the large car park P10, a wide, paved, and asphalted walking path (approx. 600 metres, about 10 minutes on foot) leads gently into the alpine village – the grounds are completely accessible for wheelchairs and prams, and accessible toilets are available. The world-famous autumn foliage of the Großer Ahornboden reaches its golden peak between late September and mid-October. Treat yourself to fresh buttermilk at the snack cabin and take home a piece of authentic Enger Bergkäse as a culinary souvenir.
